Description:
The oblique twin of TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam: the same torus (major radius 20, minor radius 10 about
the z axis) cut by a Villarceau plane, but this one turned by 37 degrees about the z axis so that
nothing lands on a seam.

A plane through the torus centre inclined by alpha with sin alpha = r/R = 0.5 is bitangent to the torus
and cuts it in two circles of radius 20 that cross at the two contact points. Turning the plane about
the torus axis carries the whole picture around with it, so the geometry is unchanged and only the
position on the faces moves. With the normal
  n = (0.5*cos 37, 0.5*sin 37, cos 30) = (0.3993177550, 0.3009075116, 0.8660254038)
the two contacts are at
  (11.9795326, 9.0272254, -8.6602540) and (-11.9795326, -9.0272254, 8.6602540)
that is at the azimuths 37 and 217 degrees, in the INTERIOR of the half faces of a torus that is split
in the xz plane, and away from the extreme meridians of the tube as well.

Everything else - the slab of 70 x 70 x 30 as an exact half space, the two crescents of the section
meeting at the two nodes, the exact half volume - is as described in TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam.
Running both is the whole point: if only the seam version fails, the defect is in the face splitting; if
both fail, it is the tangential contact itself.
Expected:
V(torus) = 4000*pi^2 = 39478.4176043574, area 4*pi^2*200 = 7895.6835208715,
extent -30,-30,-10 .. 30,30,10. V(slab) = 70*70*30 = 147000.

The plane passes through the centre, the point reflection p -> -p maps the torus onto itself and
exchanges the sides, so both parts are congruent and exactly half the torus:
  villarceauOblInter  2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787
  villarceauOblRest   2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787
  villarceauOblUnion  147000 + 19739.2088021787 = 166739.2088021787
Both halves must also be congruent to the halves of TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam - same volume, same area,
same edge length - since the two cases differ by a rotation about the z axis and nothing else. That is
the strongest check available here and it needs no computed value at all.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. FIXED on 2026-08-28 by the second repair of the same day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). Two things changed at once and both were needed:
the geometry became RIGHT where it was wrong, and the face partition became REPRODUCIBLE - the case is
stable over 4 runs now, so it finally carries a baseline. Before that it could not be pinned at all:
a face on a periodic surface was split in one run and left whole in the next, and a regenerate run
refused to record anything. The volume never moved even then, which is why the geometry could be
judged while the partition still wandered.

The geometry of this case was right all along - it is what proved the union defect of
TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam to be a SEAM problem, since the same union came out correctly here while it
returned its bare operands there. Only the partition had to be made reproducible.
  villarceauOblInter  19738.9255392  against the exact 2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787   1.4e-5
  villarceauOblRest   19738.9386536  against the same exact half                      1.4e-5
  villarceauOblUnion  166738.95477   against 147000 + 19739.2088021787                1.5e-6
and the two halves are congruent to the halves of the seam version to 5e-6, which they must be: the
two cases differ by a rotation about the z axis and nothing else. Both have euler 1, the pinch at the
two tangential contacts.
